judgment.observations: The reconstruction captures the workshop corner, tiered wooden shelves, wall-mounted measuring tools, and foreground kettle, bottle, and hardware trays. Its wider, more frontal framing leaves a large empty floor area and makes the foreground workbench less dominant. The reference is much denser: varied planes, chisels, saws, handles, upper-right tools, labels, and overlapping bench clutter are omitted or replaced by repetitive block forms. Wall-tool arrangements and proportions differ substantially. Shelf objects appear evenly spaced with limited overlap, whereas the reference has irregular packing and extensive occlusion. Materials are simplified into uniform tan wood and gray metal, losing the reference’s dark worn wood, patina, grain, polished edges, and varied surfaces. Visible render noise further reduces similarity.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The render appears to place the back shelves farther from the foreground bench, producing a more open room, but this may reflect camera framing and perspective. Several simplified tools appear seated on shelves, though their precise contact and support are difficult to judge. The foreground trays and blocks appear more separated and regularly arranged than the reference clutter; exact depth relationships and hidden geometry cannot be established from these views.
